user.title: Set up Update Manager
user.description: Update Manager applies local, semver-aware staging rules to your Home Assistant updates. Manage the staging rules afterwards on Update Manager's own "Update Manager" sidebar panel, under its Settings tab.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Update Manager is already set up. Only one instance is needed.

github_link_expired.title: Update Manager's GitHub link has expired
github_link_expired.description:
Your linked GitHub account, used to submit community votes on updates, is no longer valid (it was either revoked or hasn't been used in over 6 months). Open the Update Manager panel's Settings tab and re-link your GitHub account to keep voting.

This doesn't affect update staging or auto-install, only community voting.

confirm.title: Stop waiting for {entity_id}?
confirm.description:
{entity_id} has been installing for over {minutes} minutes without finishing. This won't cancel the install itself, which may still finish on its own. It only lets other updates that were waiting behind it continue.

Don't do this unless you're fairly sure it's actually stuck, not just slow.

confirm.title: Stop waiting for {entity_id}?
confirm.description:
{entity_id} has been installing for over {minutes} minutes without finishing. Battery-powered Zigbee devices often need to be woken up (for example by pressing a button on the device) before the update can actually start. Try that first if you haven't already.

This won't cancel the install itself, which may still finish on its own. It only lets other updates that were waiting behind it continue.
